headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill aims to reduce residential electricity costs by shifting certain grid infrastructure and capacity costs onto large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor-Chapter 1123 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas.
opponents: Data center industry, large manufacturers, Dominion Energy.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's tweaks weaken the original intent of the bill, which aimed to save residential customers approximately $5.52 a month by increasing high-load customers' bills by about 15%.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water providers to data centers to report their monthly or quarterly water consumption to the State Water Control Board, including reclaimed water.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Data Centers' Water Use: Fight for Transparency.
news_summary: The Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill mandating data centers to report their water usage to the State Water Control Board, citing concerns about the Potomac River region's water supply potentially failing to meet needs by 2030. The bill aims to provide transparency on data center water consumption, which is currently lacking, to help environmental and water advocates address the impact of data center sprawl in Virginia.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on residential areas and schools, and allows localities to require assessments on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Thomas.
news_headline: Data Centers Must Assess Noise, Environmental Impacts.
news_summary: HB 153 requires data centers to provide localities with a noise impact assessment for nearby residential areas and schools. Additionally, localities may require site assessments covering impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests, aiming to enhance transparency and mitigate negative community effects.
